title: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and “turbo cancer”
canonical_claim: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines cause turbo cancer

variants.claim: Pfizer COVID-19 mRNA vaccine induces 'turbo cancer'
COVID vaccines raise the risk of multiple cancers
mRNA vaccines cause turbo cancer and are purely harmful

evidence.summary: Some observational studies and case reports describe cancer diagnoses or cancer-related signals following COVID-19 vaccination, but the retrieved evidence does not establish a causal relationship or demonstrate a distinct clinical phenomenon called turbo cancer.

sources.finding: Reported increased one-year hazard ratios for several cancer diagnoses among vaccinated individuals.
sources.limitation: Observational association does not establish causation.

sources.finding: Reported a modest association with cancer hospitalization in some analyses.
sources.limitation: Association changed with lag-time assumptions; authors reported possible healthy-vaccinee bias and unmeasured confounding.

sources.finding: Identified case reports and population-level reports of cancers occurring temporally after vaccination or infection.
sources.limitation: Temporal association and case reports cannot establish causation.

sources.finding: Identified possible structural sampling bias capable of inflating cancer-risk associations in retrospective cohorts.
sources.limitation: Methodological critique rather than direct causal-effect study.

sources.finding: Commentary on the South Korean cohort.
sources.limitation: No abstract retrieved; conclusion not inferred.

divergence.baseline: Observational cancer signals exist, but the retrieved evidence does not establish that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines cause rapidly developing cancers or a distinct turbo-cancer phenomenon.
divergence.interpretation: The most important divergence occurs when a limited observational signal is transformed into categorical causal and universal-harm language.

priority.label: WATCH
priority.rationale: The narrative diverges from the retrieved evidence, but no explicit behavioral intention was detected in the analyzed posts.

method_note: Deep Analysis combines observed cultural diffusion, semantic variation, scientific evidence retrieval, Meme–Evidence Divergence, and explicit behavioral-intention detection.
